title: How to Remove Emotional Scars, or How to Give Yourself an Emotional Facelift
coreMove: Emotional scars heal when you keep their useful protection, drop the rigid shell, and separate old wounds from the self-image you carry today.

exampleSpecs.audience: clinicians who stop speaking after embarrassment
exampleSpecs.stakes: A nurse's silence could hide a patient-care issue.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the skin cut and scar tissue analogy to separate useful protection from frozen silence.

exampleSpecs.audience: students who hear comments as verdicts
exampleSpecs.stakes: A small joke could derail a needed design revision.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show inner size making a chance remark less threatening.

exampleSpecs.audience: team leads who wait to receive warmth before giving it
exampleSpecs.stakes: The tone of one reply may reset or inflame an angry thread.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Send approval and understanding outward before demanding it back.

exampleSpecs.audience: teachers who over-identify with a poor lesson
exampleSpecs.stakes: A bad quiz could become a verdict instead of useful feedback.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use I failed versus I am a failure to preserve correction.

exampleSpecs.audience: directors who hide all vulnerable material
exampleSpecs.stakes: A grant packet needs contact and trust without careless exposure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast thick skin with an oyster shell that blocks creative living.

exampleSpecs.audience: owners carrying old betrayal into present work
exampleSpecs.stakes: A stale grudge is shaping a current business call.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show forgiveness as release, not approval of the original harm.
